newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia to study new rail link with Angola.
newsitem.headline: Namibia to study new rail link with Angola.

text.p: Namibia is planning to build a rail link with Angola that could make its Walvis Bay port a rival to Cape Town, Durban and Maputo, a government minister said on Wednesday.

Dr Klaus Dierks, Deputy Minister of Works, Transport and Communications, told Reuters the U.S. Trade Development Agency agreed last week to fund a feasibility study at a cost of between one and two million dollars.
He said the proposal was to link Walvis Bay and the Angolan port of Namibe.
"The idea is to create a Walvis Bay to Namibe development corridor along the lines of the already existing Maputo corridor," he said.
The Maputo corridor is a joint venture between South Africa and Mozambique to develop a road and rail link and concentrate industrial development along it.

"Walvis Bay has the potential to be the main harbour on the west coast of Southern Africa, and could operate in direct competition with Maputo, Durban and Cape Town because of its closer proximity to the north-western continents," Dierks said.
He said the project would be one of the main topics on the agenda for Namibian President Sam Nujoma's upcoming three-day state visit to Angola.
He said the first phase of the project would be to build a railway line from Tsumeb to Oshikango on the Angolan border at an estimated cost of 300 million Namibian dollars.
The link would then be extended to the southern Angolan port of Namibe and to Chamutete near Cassinga in the south-west of the country which has some of the biggest iron ore mines in southern Africa.

Dierks said he was confident of Angolan support for the trade and development corridor, which would be supported by the Southern African Transport and Communications Committee (SATCC) of the Southern African Development Community.
"I am confident, and I think this initiative should be brought to fruition under a joint technical committee within the next five years," he said.
Apart from the construction of railway lines, the roads and telecommunications as well as the electricity supply network are to be upgraded under the project .
In line with the government's commitment to job-creation, most of the construction work will be labour intensive.
Namibia has been promoting Walvis Bay as a viable export and import harbour for neighbouring countries and is currently spending 60 million dollars on deepening and upgrading the port.
Namibia has also expanded its road network into neighbouring countries.
